messages:
sam: Quick proposal — instead of creating per-tenant long-lived NATs for Private deployments, we spin up a regional egress resolver that maintains a small pool of sticky egress IPs and maps tenant flows to them. goal: fewer allocated IPs, simpler auditability, easier reuse across bursts. thoughts?
priya: can you sketch failure/leak scenarios? curious about customer isolation and correlation risk. :thinking:
mike: latency-wise this sounds fine for most workloads, but what about customers who currently rely on a stable per-tenant IP for allowlisting? we'd need an option to pin a tenant to a dedicated IP.
sam: agreed — plan is to support two modes: "pinned" (1:1 tenant->ip) and "pooled" (many tenants share pool, sticky for session TTL). default to pooled to save IPs. pinned available as paid/reserved option.
kate: operational impact? how do we route e.g. when a region saturates? do we failover to another region's pool or fallback to per-tenant reserved path?
sam: proposal: per-region allocator with cross-region overflow. policy order: local pooled IP -> pinned IP if configured -> overflow to sibling region -> degrade to fallthrough Gateway (with explicit audit tag). That gives graceful degradation and traceability.
priya: what about observability/audit? we need end-to-end mapping logs for compliance: tenant_id -> allocated_ip -> stable_session_id -> timestamp. where do we store that?
mike: lightweight approach: append logs to control-plane event stream (kafka) and index the last N mappings in redis for quick lookups. full history in object storage for audits.
kate: any new attack surface? if many tenants share pool does that increase chance of IP-based rate-limits affecting others?
sam: yes. We'll add per-tenant token bucket shaping at the egress allocator, and an opt-in per-tenant hard-isolation knob that enforces dedicated pin. Also surface per-ip owner metrics so ops can quickly see which tenant is impacted.
priya: how about TLS client certs or allowlists that depend on stable source IP? pinned addresses cover that, but switching from pinned->pooled must require customer ok and a migration window.
mike: rollout plan idea: alpha with a few internal tenants, then beta with small customers who agree to pooled. we should expose a compatibility probe endpoint that customers can hit to validate their allowlist: `curl https://egress-check.internal/tenant/ID` returns current egress ip + mapping TTL.
infra-bot: NOTE: provisioning model will need new quota API. estimate: allocator service + region pool controller + short-lived lease store. suggest 2 small ECS tasks per region + autoscale policy.
kate: cost model? likely saves IP allocation charges on cloud side but adds runtime infra costs. need showback to finance.
sam: agreed. I'll draft an RFC with: problem statement, modes (pinned/pooled), mapping lifecycle, audit design, failure modes, rollout plan, API samples, and migration checklist. want volunteers to review before I publish.
priya: I can take audit + compliance section.
mike: I'll do perf & rate-limit sim numbers.
kate: I'll own rollout/playbook + ops runbook.
sam: thanks — I'll post RFC in #architecture next week. tagging @kate for follow-up on runbook. :thumbsup:
